title: dsh joins the review check as a fourth reviewer
summary: Adds DeepSeek Harness (dsh) as a fourth reviewer alongside codex, claude and opencode. dsh is now started directly as `dsh --profile headless` with the prompt on standard input — no shell wrapper on any platform — and is held to read-only file writes by `DSH_PERMISSION_MODE=read-only` in its environment, so it no longer counts as a reviewer with no read-only mode. A new `review-dsh` CI job runs it in the pinned review container with only `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, a seven-host egress allow-list that adds `api.deepseek.com`, and a check that the image carries dsh 0.2.0-rc.2; the final reduce job now waits on it too.

nodes.label: review-check.yml
nodes.subtitle: reusable workflow
nodes.summary: Holds every job of the review check. This change adds the `review-dsh` job, pins `DSH_VERSION`, declares the `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` secret and adds `review-dsh` to the final job's `needs`.

nodes.label: build job
nodes.summary: Builds osf from the workflow's trusted commit, finds the work item and uploads both as artifacts. Holds no secret.

nodes.label: review codex
nodes.summary: Runs the codex reviewer in the review container with its own sandbox bypassed, holding only `OPENAI_API_KEY`.

nodes.label: review claude
nodes.summary: Runs the claude reviewer in the review container, holding only `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`.

nodes.label: review opencode
nodes.summary: Runs the opencode reviewer in the review container, holding only `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`.

nodes.label: review dsh
nodes.subtitle: new reviewer job
nodes.summary: New job. Blocks egress to seven hosts (the six GitHub/registry hosts plus `api.deepseek.com`), checks `dsh --version` against the pinned `DSH_VERSION`, then runs `osf review run --reviewer dsh --if-enabled` in the review container with only `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` in the environment and `/pr`, `/base` and `/work-item` mounted read-only. Saves `out/dsh.json` as the `review-run-dsh` artifact.

nodes.label: review (reduce)
nodes.summary: Runs `osf review reduce` over the saved answers and posts the result. Its `needs` list now includes `review-dsh`, so a missing dsh answer counts as could-not-run.

nodes.label: osf review run
nodes.subtitle: --reviewer <name>
nodes.summary: Starts the named reviewer with its command, environment and read-only switches, writes the prompt to its standard input and reads the answer back. Now starts dsh directly instead of through `sh -c`.

nodes.label: AGENTS
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/agents.rs
nodes.summary: The static list of agents. dsh's command becomes `["dsh", "--profile", "headless"]` and its review gains `read_only: Some(ReadOnly { env: [("DSH_PERMISSION_MODE", "read-only")] })`.

nodes.label: dsh entry
nodes.subtitle: family deepseek
nodes.summary: DeepSeek Harness. No longer wrapped in a shell; reads its prompt from standard input and is confined to read-only file writes by `DSH_PERMISSION_MODE`. Takes no schema flag and no model flag, so the prompt asks for the JSON answer.

nodes.label: osf.toml roster
nodes.summary: `reviewers` becomes `["codex", "claude", "opencode", "dsh"]`. The comment records that dsh's family is the builder's own, so a dsh-built change leaves it out.

nodes.label: agents.rs tests
nodes.summary: Replaces `dsh_documents_no_read_only_mode` with tests that every reviewing agent documents a read-only or container mode, that dsh uses `DSH_PERMISSION_MODE=read-only`, that no agent starts through a shell, and that dsh runs its headless profile.

nodes.label: review_workflow.rs
nodes.summary: New tests tie the workflow's reviewer jobs to the roster in osf.toml, check the dsh version pin, the single provider secret, the seven-host allow-list and the absence of the codex bypass in the dsh job.

nodes.label: api.deepseek.com
nodes.summary: dsh's model provider, the default base URL of its DeepSeek route. Added to the dsh job's egress allow-list.

nodes.label: GitHub + ghcr.io
nodes.summary: The six hosts every reviewer job needs: github.com, api.github.com, codeload.github.com, objects.githubusercontent.com, ghcr.io and pkg-containers.githubusercontent.com.

edges.label: osf-binary, work-item
edges.summary: The dsh job needs the build job and downloads the osf binary and the work item it saved.

edges.label: review-run-dsh
edges.summary: The final job now waits on the dsh job and reads its saved answer; a missing answer counts as could-not-run.

edges.label: osf review run --reviewer dsh
edges.summary: The job runs osf inside the review container with the pull request tree mounted read-only.

edges.label: model calls
edges.summary: The only provider host the dsh job allows; every other egress is blocked.

edges.label: checkout, registry
edges.summary: The job checks out base and head, logs in to ghcr.io and pulls the pinned review image.

edges.label: command, env, read_only
edges.summary: osf looks the reviewer up in the agent list and applies its command, environment and read-only switches.
The dsh entry is the one this change rewrites.

edges.label: reviewers
edges.summary: The roster now names dsh, so a dsh job exists and osf will start it.
Unit tests assert dsh's command, environment and the no-shell rule across the whole list.
Integration tests read the workflow text and check the dsh job against the roster and the pinned version.
